newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine oil firms seen losing money.
newsitem.headline: Philippine oil firms seen losing money.

text.p: The Philippines Department of Energy said local oil refiners were likely to incur losses if crude oil prices which reached four-month highs on Tuesday persisted at those levels for long.

Domestic oil prices will not be immediately affected as Singapore Posted Prices, the basis of a newly implemented automatic oil price formula, remain steady, the department's assistant director Aida Pujanes said.
"But there will be losses for oil firms if the increasing crude cost will continue to hold," Pujanes said.
"Because of the time lag, there is no immediate impact on Singapore Postings and therefore on local prices," she added.
Oil company officials said they could not pass on the additional cost since the automatic oil price formula does not take into account crude costs but Singapore Postings.

Oil prices were under full government control until last month when the first phase of an oil deregulation programme began under which oil firms are allowed to adjust their prices but only up to a certain extent.
Before deregulation started, the government ran a buffer fund which reimbursed losses incurred by oil firms.

Crude oil prices in Asia jumped to fresh four-month highs on Tuesday after the United States launched a cruise missile strike on Iraq in retaliation for Iraqi military attacks on Kurds in the north of the country.
The benchmark U.S. light crude oil for October delivery rose to $23.75 per barrel from $23.48 per barrel in the minutes that followed the Pentagon's announcement during Tokyo afternoon trade.

There are three oil firms in the Philippines. They are Petron Corp, which is 40 percent owned by Saudi Arabia's Aramco, Caltex Philippines Inc, a unit of U.S.-based Chevron Corp and Texaco Inc and Pilipinas Shell, a unit of the Royal Dutch/Shell group.
